name: Employer-Sponsored Work Permit

requirements.blocker_text: A Cameroonian employer must initiate and sponsor the work-permit application with the Ministry of Labor and Social Security. Once approved, the foreign worker applies for a long-stay visa at a Cameroonian embassy or consulate to enter and begin employment. Required: employment contract, job description, certified qualifications, company registration documents, medical certificate, and CV. No quota or labor-market-test procedure was found described in the sources reached. Processing commonly takes 4-6 months end to end. A short-stay (tourist) visa explicitly does not permit local employment.
requirements.fix_path: Secure a job offer from a Cameroonian employer willing to sponsor the Ministry of Labor application, then apply for the long-stay visa once approved.

sources.title: Rivermate -- Ministry of Labor and Social Security process, document requirements, timeline, employer-sponsorship structure

STATUS: DRAFT -- no primary Ministry of Labor decree text could be located and fetched in this build, so this rests on a tier-3 relocation-services guide. pr_after_months (24) and citizenship_after_months (60) modeled from Cameroon's general residence-card ladder and naturalization framework (see cm_long_term_residence.json and cm_citizenship_naturalisation.json, both tier-2 confirmed directly from the 1997 Foreigners Law and 1968 Nationality Code respectively), not from a work-permit-specific accelerated provision -- flagged as this dataset's own inference rather than a directly stated rule for this route specifically. family_can_join set to true since Cameroon's Foreigners Law (Loi 1997/012) grants dependent children of a resident-card holder automatic derivative card status while living with and dependent on that parent (see cm_long_term_residence.json for the direct citation).
